extraction.name: XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in “universal” speech representation learning.

extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark aggregates existing publicly available speech datasets (Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and creates new splits. Fleurs was created by collecting 1-3 recordings for each of 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages. Other datasets were sourced from existing corpora like Librivox, European Parliament sessions, and e-banking domains.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs (newly collected recordings of FLoRes sentences), Multilingual LibriSpeech (read audiobooks from Librivox), VoxPopuli (European Parliament sessions), CoVoST-2 (speech translation corpus), Minds-14 (e-banking intent data).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Datasets were merged into multilingual training sets (e.g., Minds-14). Train-dev-test splits were created for Fleurs (1509, 150, 350 sentences). For speech retrieval, the pool of transcription candidates was augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Scripts are provided to download and reproduce preprocessing steps. For speech retrieval, fixed-size embeddings are used. For classification, average results over 5 random seeds are encouraged. Hyperparameter tuning is performed on the dev set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are derived from existing datasets: transcriptions for ASR/ST, intent labels for Minds-14, and language IDs for Fleurs-LangID. Fleurs recordings were collected for parallel sentences.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made accessible through the HuggingFace platform. Updates to Fleurs (e.g., missing or low-quality recordings) are expected in a 2nd version.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet. The benchmark aims to build better speech representations in many languages and enable rapid access to data-efficient speech technology for all the world’s languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results show discrepancies between geographical groups, with better performance on Western European languages compared to Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages, explained by larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages. Overfitting on speaker ID is a noted issue for LangID tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Tasks are focused on linguistic aspects of speech; nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects (e.g., speech synthesis, voice conversion) are not evaluated. Test sets are not hidden, which risks overfitting. Performance gaps exist across language families due to data imbalance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of multilingual speech representation learning models. Evaluation of cross-lingual transfer learning.
